clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country to buy an apple orchard in March 1952, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, her distance from Walter as he worked long hours, Glen's fights at school, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June keeping to her bed for weeks that winter, rows between Walter and June over money for new trees. By September 1953 June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, settling the period. Walter's sister Faye's stomach aches fall in these months but cannot be dated to the year, so the period holds only the shifts that can be placed.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily, he and Glen blamed each other, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Glen's son Roy's asthma attacks worsened that winter, Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969, Ida's heart trouble was found. By October 1969 Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, settling the period. Roy's asthma eased once spring came; that lift comes with Nora's symptom rising, so the two are one movement.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the months that follow: Glen sat out in the truck for hours, he and Marian fought loud fights at night over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight, Nora kept to her room and distanced from her mother, Walter drank again after six years off it. By June 1976 Nora was eating again and made the track team, settling the period. Glen's move to the delivery truck in March 1976 falls within this settling.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into Nora and Sam's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma, Sam's widowed mother, selling her farm and moving into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990, within the months that follow: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals, Sam worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, Sam took his mother's side, Nora's son Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flared on both hands, Nora and Sam had rows most nights. By June 1991 when Wilma took a flat in town, Nora's eczema cleared over the summer, settling the period.
